fields.name: Sūryānanda (Galtā)
fields.place: Galtā (Jaipur, Rajasthan); Gopīvallabhapura; died at Purī
fields.disciples: Raghunātha dāsa of Galtā (later its mahānta)
fields.notes: Head abbot of the Galtā seat of the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas (Jaipur). Cursed his disciple Raghunātha dāsa with leprosy and promised to cure him in his next life. At Gopīvallabhapura, with Śyāmānanda's and Rasikānanda's blessing, asked to be reborn in Rasikānanda's family; died at Purī and was born as Nayanānanda (#2006), eldest son of Rādhānanda, by whose foot-water Raghunātha was healed.

An unlettered brāhmaṇa who recited the whole Bhagavad-gītā daily in the Raṅganātha temple, mispronouncing it, by his guru's order, seeing Kṛṣṇa as Arjuna's charioteer. Lord Caitanya, then at Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa's house for the Cāturmāsya, told him he had understood the Gītā, embraced him and revealed Himself; he stayed with the Lord for the four months (CC Madhya 9.93-103).

fields.works: Āmoda-kāvya (15 chapters on Kṛṣṇa-līlā); Sāmañjasa (vṛtti); Vidvad-vinodinī Sūcikā (on the Bhāgavatam); Sītā-śataka-kāvya; Sannyāsa-vṛtti
fields.notes: Son of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa; a scholar of Kāśī in the assembly of Kāśīnātha (first principal of the Sanskrit College, 1791-1801), titled Tarkālaṅkāra and Vidyābahādur. Revered Lord Caitanya and His associates, but in siddhānta followed Sītā-Rāma and the Rāmānandīs (dvaita, not acintya-bhedābheda).
